commenter: Jen Sisson, CEO, International Corporate Governance Network (ICGN)

quotes.quote: We strongly oppose the changes which result in the removal of the auditor attestation requirement under Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes Oxley Act (SOX) for companies other than large accelerated filers.
We therefore urge the Commission to retain the auditor attestation requirement for all reporting companies that are currently subject to Section 404(b).

Raising the Large Accelerated Filer threshold from US$700 million to US$2 billion would place most public companies into a much more fragmented disclosure regime and significantly reduce the information that must be made available to investors.
We do not support the proposed 60-month seasoning period before Large Accelerated Filer status can apply and instead recommend retaining the current 12-month period.

notes: Filed under S7-2026-17 (Registered Offering Reform) but the letter expressly covers both S7-2026-17 and S7-2026-18 and has a full S7-2026-18 section (pp. 3-10); coded normally, not_a_comment=false. Investor association (led by investors with >US$100tn AUM) -> investor. do_not_expand: asks to keep 404(b) for every company now subject to it, i.e. no widening. view_2bn coded oppose_any_increase: objects to raising LAF line from $700m to $2bn and says filer status reforms 'go too far'; it does not literally say 'keep $700m', so flag if the other coder chose null. Notes FPI/domestic inconsistency (p.6: attestation still applies to some FPIs above $75m float) but uses it as an argument against the domestic exemption, not a request to extend relief to FPIs -> fpi_parity=false. Cites GAO-13-582 (attestation disclosure) only as a source; no disclosure ask -> asks_disclosure=false. 'If the Commission proceeds... transition arrangements should apply' plus SEC monitoring/reinstatement process (p.7) is not interim relief or company guidance. 'Targeted accommodations for the smallest companies may be appropriate' (p.3) is generic and not tied to the attestation, so not read as accepting some widening (not too_broad).

commenter: Marc I. Steinberg, Radford Chair and Professor of Law (Southern Methodist University)

quotes.quote: I write this comment letter in my individual capacity.
It rescinds the application of key provisions of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act for the vast majority of Exchange Act reporting companies (I understand roughly 80% of Exchange Act reporting companies).

notes: Silent on the attestation: the letter objects to rescinding 'key provisions of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act' but never names Section 404(b), the auditor attestation or the exemption; its named examples are say-on-pay and pay-versus-performance (exec comp, not 404(b)). Flag for adjudication: a reader could treat the generic SOX reference as addressing 404(b), in which case it would be do_not_expand. Constituency coded individual because he states he writes 'in my individual capacity' (codebook: individual = person writing in a personal capacity); academic is the plausible alternative (SMU law letterhead, signs as professor) - flag. Letter dated May 27, 2026; docket date June 1, 2026. Supports simplifying disclosure generally. Commenter name in docket header misspells 'Radford' as 'Radforf'.

commenter: Thomas A. Ciccone, Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Broadwind, Inc.

quotes.quote: Broadwind respectfully urges the Commission to adopt the Proposed Filer Rules substantially as proposed and, while the rulemaking remains pending, to provide an optional one-time transition accommodation for issuers that would otherwise newly become accelerated filers

Broadwind and these similarly situated registrants are already incurring significant costs to responsibly prepare for shortened filing deadlines, auditor attestation requirements, staffing additions, external advisor costs, and related compliance obligations

providing an optional, one-time transition period—such as a 12-month implementation grace period—during which affected registrants could defer the application of a newly triggered accelerated filer or large accelerated filer status

notes: Addresses the attestation via the cost of preparing for 'auditor attestation requirements' on becoming an accelerated filer, and notes 404(a) management report would still apply (p.2). Supports adoption substantially as proposed -> support. Interim relief: SRC/NAF with float >$75m expecting to become an accelerated filer at FYE 2026; asks for 12-month grace period before a final rule. Suggests issuers relying on the transition accommodation disclose that election (p.3); that is disclosure of the relief election, not of whether an attestation was obtained -> asks_disclosure=false (flag). Grace period is transition relief, not a different threshold -> names_alternative=false. Mentions revenue >$100m only as a fact about itself; no revenue test proposed. Page 4 blank.
